questions.instructions: Choose the single dominant Type of record from the French Ebola coding framework. Definitions: Observations, perceptions ou croyances = statements of what the person observes, believes, perceives or fears (including rumours, mistrust and suspicion); Questions = the person asks something; Suggestions = the person proposes how something should be done or changed; Appréciations = thanks, praise, encouragement; Demandes = the person asks for information, services, items, treatment or action; Signalements et préoccupations = report of a specific problem, complaint, stigma or incident needing attention; Allégations et Signalement d’incident = allegation of misconduct by response actors (corruption, nepotism, discrimination, illegal consumption, SEA) or report of an incident linked to such conduct. If the feedback is incomplete, unintelligible or fits nowhere, use the Type whose catch-all code applies best (Autres observations, perceptions ou croyances / Autres questions / Autre demande). Use record.type_of_feedback only as supporting context and verify it against record.Feedback. Use the configured French coding framework exactly (Type > Catégorie > Sous-code > Code); do not invent, shorten, translate or correct labels. If several themes are present, prioritize an immediate safeguarding, safety or public-health concern; otherwise choose the dominant speech act and theme. Return one exact configured label.

Choose the single exact Code (French leaf code) that best describes record, within the accepted Type in decisions.feedback_type. The available options are restricted to that Type. Each option description gives its exact Type, Catégorie, Sous-code and Code; use this context to distinguish the options. The category and sub-code will be filled from the selected code’s exact framework mapping.

questions.instructions: Classify handling sensitivity independently from whether the feedback is true. Use the ordered rubric from lowest to highest.

options.label: Not sensitive
options.description: Ordinary feedback without a protection, safety, safeguarding, confidentiality or identifiable-person concern.

options.label: Sensitive
options.description: Non-identifying allegation of misconduct, corruption, discrimination, stigma, protection concern, access barrier, conflict or security concern.

options.label: Highly sensitive / confidential
options.description: Possible SEA, safeguarding concern, personally identifiable information, targeted threat, violence, immediate risk to a person, individual medical information or serious identifiable allegation.

questions.instructions: Assess operational urgency independently from sensitivity and without assuming the feedback is true. Use the ordered rubric from lowest to highest.

options.label: Low
options.description: Praise, routine comment, non-urgent suggestion or incomplete feedback without an identified risk.

options.label: Medium
options.description: Question, request, concern or belief requiring a response or verification without immediate danger.

options.label: High
options.description: Serious access barrier, misconduct allegation, collective refusal, dangerous mistrust, severe stigma or an issue likely to disrupt the response.

options.label: Critical / Urgent
options.description: Suspected case or death requiring an immediate public-health alert, possible SEA or serious safeguarding issue, imminent threat or violence, or immediate risk to a person.

questions.instructions: Return New when the record contains enough substantive information to assign a specific Type, Catégorie, Sous-code and Code from the French Ebola coding framework. Return Needs review when the interaction is interrupted, abusive, withdrawn, blocked by a communication barrier, otherwise incomplete or unintelligible, or can only be coded with a catch-all code (Autres… / Autre…) because it falls outside the framework. Return one exact configured label.
Choose the single most appropriate first operational action for record. Prioritize safeguarding, safety and public-health alerts when relevant. Do not claim that an action has already occurred.
Choose the sector with primary responsibility for the first response to record. If several sectors are relevant, select the one that must act first.

Choose the overall sentiment expressed in record.Feedback. Return Positive for appreciation, approval, hope or encouragement; Negative for fear, anger, mistrust, dissatisfaction, allegations, complaints or harmful beliefs; Neutral for factual statements, straightforward questions or requests without a clear emotional tone; Mixed when both positive and negative sentiment are materially present; Unclear when the feedback is incomplete, incoherent or does not provide enough information to determine sentiment. Classify the tone expressed by the feedback provider, not whether the statement is factually true. Return one exact configured label.

report.title: Ebola community feedback coding report
report.instructions: Summarize the classified community feedback using exact counts and proportions. Highlight critical or sensitive feedback, dominant types, categories, sub-codes and codes of the French Ebola coding framework. Highlight routing actions, sector patterns, sentiment and records whose status is Needs review. Do not treat allegations or beliefs as verified facts.
